newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF head says Russia has to spend better, not less.
newsitem.headline: IMF head says Russia has to spend better, not less.

text.p: Russia has to spend its budget revenues in a more effective way to cut the budget deficit, Izvestia newspaper on Thursday quoted International Monetary Fund chairman Michel Camdessus as saying.
"The problem is that budget spending must be done better, it is not supposed to be made much smaller," Camdessus said.

He said Russia's budget deficit had to be small enough for the central bank not to cover the gap in an inflationary way. "Efforts should be focused on income collection," he said, adding that the IMF was worried about tax evasion in Russia.
"Democracy assumes that the people agree to pay taxes. High tax debt in Russia is close to a crisis of democracy. History showed...that this may lead to anarchy or dictatorship."
Camdessus also said he hoped Russia and IMF would approve a joint economic programme for 1997-1998 soon.

Camdessus is visiting Russia for talks with the new government team and Interfax news agency on Thursday quoted him as saying that the IMF may release the next tranche of its $10 billion three-year loan to Russia by the end of this month.
The IMF has delayed some tranches of the loan due to concern over low tax revenues.
